rows: Offensive realism: China seeking regional hegemony; US resisting. Security dilemma: each side's defensive measures threaten the other. Power shift: China approaching parity in regional military capability.
Why is Taiwan strategically critical beyond ideology?

TSMC produces ~90% of world's advanced chips. Military conflict = global semiconductor supply disruption. This is why CHIPS Act and fab diversification are security policy, not just industrial policy.
What changed in European security after 2022?

Finland/Sweden joined NATO (NATO now borders Russia extensively). Germany reversed 75 years of military restraint (Zeitenwende). Defense spending commitments accelerated across alliance. EU defense integration gained real momentum.

Middle powers (India, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Brazil) refuse to choose between US and China. They extract concessions from both, maintain autonomy, and align selectively based on interest. This complicates US alliance management and sanctions enforcement.

Evidence mostly says no: most BRI loans are commercial; China has renegotiated more than seized assets; Sri Lanka's crisis was bonds-driven. The real problems are project quality and political influence, not strategic asset seizure.
What is the autonomous weapons accountability problem?

No clear legal answer to who is criminally/legally responsible if an autonomous system commits a war crime. The laws of armed conflict require accountability; autonomous systems break the human-in-the-loop assumption.
Tooze's framework: simultaneous, interacting crises (climate, pandemic, geopolitical, democratic) that compound each other, stressing governance systems designed to handle one crisis at a time.
How does AI affect disinformation in IR?

Scale: automated account networks, LLM text generation, deepfake media; speed: false narratives spread before correction; targeting: microtargeting of specific populations. No adequate governance framework exists internationally.
